samples.summary: The new "only `push` is guarded, app redirects are `replace`" contract rests on a premise that is false at the one call site it names: `PrivateRoute` redirects with a **push**, not a replace.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/PrivateRoute.tsx:32 renders `<Navigate to="/login" />` with no `replace` prop — react-router's `<Navigate>` defaults to `replace={false}`, i.e. `navigator.push`. The provider's new comment (navigation-guard-provider.tsx:148-155), the design doc (docs/design/sync-status.md:307-310) and the new test (tests/components/navigation-guard/navigation-guard.test.tsx, `<Link to="/login" replace>`) all assert that this redirect is a `replace` and therefore unrefusable. It is not: it enters the guarded `push` path, so a registered guard can hold it, and because the new code drops the navigation entirely when the user answers *Stay* (and never re-issues it — `<Navigate>` fires once in an effect), the session-expiry redirect would be swallowed for good, exactly the failure the comment says the replace exemption prevents. `PublicRoute.tsx:21` (`<Navigate to="/" />`) is the same shape. Reachability depends on whether the editor subtree (which owns the guard, via `SyncStatusChip` under PrivateRoute's `<Outlet>`) has already unregistered in the same commit; the fix belongs on PrivateRoute/PublicRoute (`replace`) or on the exemption's wording, and the test should exercise the real `<Navigate>` rather than a hand-written `replace` link.

verdict.reason: Every claimed location checks out. PrivateRoute.tsx:32 renders `<Navigate to="/login" />` with no `replace` prop, and PublicRoute.tsx:21 renders `<Navigate to="/" />` likewise; with BrowserRouter (App.tsx:1,95) and react-router-dom ^7.18.2 (package.json:76), `<Navigate>` defaults to replace=false and therefore dispatches through `navigator.push`, i.e. the newly guarded path at navigation-guard-provider.tsx:118-135. The new comment (navigation-guard-provider.tsx:148-155), the design doc (docs/design/sync-status.md:304-310) and the new test (navigation-guard.test.tsx:52-55,159-170, which uses a hand-written `<Link to="/login" replace>` rather than the real `<Navigate>`) all assert that PrivateRoute's /login redirect is an unrefusable `replace`. Every other self-redirect in the app does use `replace` (document-detail.tsx:863, docs-detail.tsx:342, slides-detail.tsx:947, notes-detail.tsx:369, board-detail.tsx:252, file-detail.tsx:242,247, home-or-redirect.tsx:26), so PrivateRoute/PublicRoute are the two sites out of step with the invariant the provider relies on. The guard owner (sync-status-chip.tsx:115 via use-navigation-guard.ts:54-57) lives inside PrivateRoute's Outlet subtree (App.tsx:128-176), so a live guard can meet this push; nothing in the repo guards against it — the only mitigation is React's effect-ordering during the unmount commit, which is an inference about React internals rather than a citable guard, so I cannot claim already-guarded. This is a contract/invariant violation at call sites outside the diff, squarely in the blast-radius lane; it is real and, with a session-expiry redirect potentially held and then dropped on "Stay" (plus the history-stack/Back difference push introduces), blocking at major.

finding.summary: `leaving()` compares a basename-joined destination against a basename-stripped current location, so under a non-"/" VITE_FRONTEND_BASENAME every guarded navigation (including same-document query rewrites) is treated as leaving
finding.evidence: `pathOf(navigator, to)` delegates to `history.createHref`, which does NOT prepend the router basename (react-router's `Router` only joins the basename inside `useNavigate`: it calls `navigator.push(joinPaths([basename, path.pathname]))`). The current location comes from `useLocation()`, which is basename-STRIPPED. So with basename `/wafflebase`, `pathOf(base, to)` = `/wafflebase/s/doc-1` while `pathOf(base, locationRef.current)` = `/s/doc-1`, and `next !== current` is always true. Non-"/" basenames are a supported, documented deployment: packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:381 ("Only if not served at /") and .github/workflows/publish-ghpage.yml:167 (`VITE_FRONTEND_BASENAME: ${{ vars.VITE_FRONTEND_BASENAME || '/' }}`). The doc comment on `pathOf` claims "basename included" for both sides; only the tests' MemoryRouter (basename "/") exercises the equal case, which is why the suite is green. Fix belongs in the new code (strip the basename from `to`, or compare against `base.createHref(locationRef.current)` after joining the basename).

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. `leaving()` does NOT compare a basename-joined destination against a basename-stripped location: navigation-guard-provider.tsx:115 compares `pathOf(base, to)` against `basenamed(context.basename, pathname)`, and `basenamed` (:49-51) re-joins the router basename onto the `useLocation()` pathname using react-router's own join/collapse semantics (`[basename, pathname].join("/").replace(/\/\/+/g, "/")`), so `/` collapses away and `/app` + `/s/doc-1` yields `/app/s/doc-1`. The `pathOf` doc comment (:32-38) states the exact opposite of what the finding quotes — it says `createHref` does *not* prepend the basename and that comparison requires the same join "see `basenamed`". The basename is available on the context because App.tsx:95 mounts `<Router basename={import.meta.env.VITE_FRONTEND_BASENAME}>` and react-router's Router puts the normalised basename in NavigationContext. The claim that only a basename-"/" MemoryRouter exercises the equal case is also false: navigation-guard.test.tsx:128-150 renders `<MemoryRouter basename="/app" initialEntries={['/app/s/doc-1']}>`, clicks `<Link to="/s/doc-1?tab=2">` with a blocking guard, and asserts no prompt. The proposed fix is already implemented in the file.

finding.summary: The editors' "Document not found" automatic redirects are now interceptable by the new guard, and if the user picks Stay the redirect is cancelled permanently (the effect never re-fires)
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-detail.tsx:159-166 runs `navigate(fallbackSlug ? \`/w/${fallbackSlug}\` : "/documents", { replace: true })` inside a `useEffect` while the same component still renders `<SiteHeader ... syncStatus>` (docs-detail.tsx:196-200), i.e. while `SyncStatusChip` has a guard registered. The patched `navigator.replace` now holds that redirect behind the "Leave without saving?" dialog; clicking Stay drops `pendingRef` and the effect's deps (`isDocumentError`, `navigate`, `fallbackSlug`) do not change, so the redirect never happens again and the user is left inside a document the server reports as missing. Same pattern at packages/frontend/src/app/documents/document-detail.tsx:229, packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-detail.tsx:183, packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-detail.tsx:161, packages/frontend/src/app/board/board-detail.tsx:125 — none of these call sites were updated to opt out of the guard.

verdict.reason: The finding's central factual premise is false: the guard does not intercept `replace`. In navigation-guard-provider.tsx:143-159 the rebuilt navigator wraps only `push` (line 157, guarded implementation at lines 118-135); `replace` at line 158 is a bare pass-through `(to, state, opts) => base.replace(to, state, opts)` that never reads `guardsRef`, never sets `pendingRef`, and never calls `setPrompt`. All five cited call sites issue their "Document not found" redirect with `replace: true` (docs-detail.tsx:162-164, document-detail.tsx:229-231, notes-detail.tsx:183-185, slides-detail.tsx:161-163, board-detail.tsx:125-127), and react-router's useNavigate dispatches those via `navigator.replace`, so they bypass the dialog entirely — there is no prompt to answer and therefore no "Stay" that could permanently cancel the effect. The provider comment at lines 148-155 documents this as the deliberate design, naming this exact 404-redirect scenario, and navigation-guard.test.tsx:159-166 is a regression test asserting a `replace` navigation is never prompted. I also confirmed no other module wraps UNSAFE_NavigationContext (grep across packages/frontend/src returns only navigation-guard-provider.tsx), so no second layer re-guards replace. The call sites correctly require no opt-out.
